title: Extend a prescribed lift across a smooth affine open over general coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a specified residue-field isomorphism $\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda\cong k$. Let $A^\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective local $\Lambda$-algebra homomorphism between commutative Artinian local $\Lambda$-algebras, with specified residue-field identifications $A^\prime/\mathfrak m_{A^\prime}\cong k$ and $A/\mathfrak m_A\cong k$ as $\Lambda$-algebras, inducing the identity on $k$. Here a local ring has exactly one maximal ideal and an Artinian ring has the descending chain condition on ideals. Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] covered by affine open subschemes $X=U\cup V$, with $U\cap V$ affine. Suppose that $U$ and $U\cap V$ are smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] with a specified special-fibre isomorphism $\iota:Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any open $W\subseteq X$, write $Y_W$ for the open subscheme corresponding to $W$ under the underlying-space homeomorphism of the nilpotent special fibre. Suppose $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime$ is flat and an $A$-isomorphism $e:Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime}\operatorname{Spec}A\cong Y_V$ is given. Then there exist a flat $A^\prime$-scheme $Y^\prime$, an $A$-isomorphism $\alpha:Y^\prime\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime}\operatorname{Spec}A\cong Y$, and an $A^\prime$-isomorphism $\gamma:Y^\prime_V\cong Z$, such that $e\circ\gamma_A=\alpha|_{Y_V}$. The special fibre of $Y^\prime$ is identified with $X$ by $\iota\circ\alpha_k$; this identification defines $Y^\prime_V$, and $\gamma_A$ denotes reduction to $A$. Empty opens, disconnected schemes and arbitrary dimensions are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0DZN (lemma-glueing-smooth), second assertion, specialized to U_1 smooth; situation-glueing and example-schemes. General coefficient category: section-general and formal-defos.tex, definition-CLambda.

proof.text: Put $W=U\cap V$, $K=\ker(A^\prime\to A)$ and $\mathfrak m^\prime=\mathfrak m_{A^\prime}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], the maximal ideals of $A$ and $A^\prime$ are nilpotent; $K\subseteq\mathfrak m^\prime$ is nilpotent too. On each affine chart, reduction by any of these ideals is $B\to B/JB$ with $JB$ nilpotent. Every prime contains $JB$, so this is a thickening and a homeomorphism by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Thus labelled opens are well defined and reduction preserves their labels. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], restrictions of a flat morphism to opens are flat, since their local structural homomorphisms are unchanged. The special fibre of $Y_U$ is the affine $U$, so [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-scheme] makes $Y_U$ affine.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth; situation-glueing and lemma-open; nilpotent opens and affine deformations

proof.text: The special fibre $U$ is smooth, hence locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-deformation-lfp] to $Y_U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the nilpotent maximal ideal of $A$: $Y_U$ is locally of finite presentation over $A$. There is just one point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with residue field $k$, and its fibre is $U$. Consequently [lem-pc-smooth-characterization] shows $Y_U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-quotient-lift] to the given surjection $A^\prime\to A$ and this affine smooth scheme, obtaining an affine smooth $A^\prime$-scheme $L$ and an $A$-isomorphism $a:L_A\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_U$. The scheme $L$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Its special fibre is labelled by $U$ using $\iota a_k$.

source.place: Tag 07M8, proposition-lift-smooth (2); examples-defos.tex lemma-lci-unobstructed specialized to the smooth U-piece; lfp ascent is More on Morphisms Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property (13)

proof.text: Let $D\subseteq L$ and $E\subseteq Z$ be the opens labelled by $W$, using $a$ and $e$ respectively. Open immersions remain open immersions under base change by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Hence $a$ and $e$ restrict to $a_W:D_A\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_W$ and $e_W:E_A\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_W$. Both $D$ and $E$ have special fibre $W$, so they are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-scheme]. They are flat because they are opens of the flat schemes $L,Z$, by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The smooth special fibre $W$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; [lem-sfb-flat-deformation-lfp] and [lem-pc-smooth-characterization], now over $A^\prime$, show that $E\to\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime$ is smooth. This uses no prior finite-presentation hypothesis on $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, matching the two affine overlap deformations; More on Morphisms Tags 06AD and 06AG

proof.text: Set $h_0=e_W^{-1}a_W:D_A\xrightarrow{\sim}E_A$ and regard its composite with $E_A\to E$ as an $A^\prime$-morphism. Write $D=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and choose $N\geq1$ with $K^N=0$. Start with this map on $D_1=\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)$. For $1\leq r<N$, the inclusion $D_r\subseteq D_{r+1}=\operatorname{Spec}(B/K^{r+1}B)$ has square-zero ideal $K^rB/K^{r+1}B$, since $2r\geq r+1$. Smoothness of $E$ gives the lifting property of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. Applying it successively yields compatible $A^\prime$-maps $D_r\to E$, ending in $h:D=D_N\to E$ with reduction $h_0$ (as a map to $E_A$ by the fibre-product property).

source.place: Tag 02H0, definition-formally-smooth; iterate its first order affine lifting condition along powers of K

proof.text: The lifted map is an isomorphism, not merely a morphism. Write $E=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $B,C$ are flat $A^\prime$-modules. The ring map $h^*:C\to B$ reduces to an isomorphism modulo $K$, hence modulo $\mathfrak m^\prime$. Choose a $k$-basis $(\bar c_i)$ of $C/\mathfrak m^\prime C$ and representatives $c_i\in C$. Their images $h^*(c_i)$ reduce to a basis of $B/\mathfrak m^\prime B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-artinian-basis-when-flat] to both flat modules over the same local ring $A^\prime$: the two chosen families are bases over $A^\prime$. The linear map $h^*$ sends one basis to the other, so its inverse sends $h^*(c_i)$ to $c_i$. Thus $h^*$ is bijective, and its inverse preserves products and the unit by applying the injective $h^*$. Therefore $h$ is an $A^\prime$-isomorphism with $e_Wh_A=a_W$. This argument includes the zero modules when $W$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 051F, lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat; basis comparison for the two flat affine overlaps

proof.text: Glue $L$ and $Z$ along $h:D\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes], with reverse transition $h^{-1}$. For two pieces every cocycle identity is an identity or $h^{-1}h=1$ or $hh^{-1}=1$. Obtain open immersions $j_L:L\to Y^\prime$ and $j_Z:Z\to Y^\prime$ whose images cover and whose intersection is exactly $D\cong E$, with $j_L|_D=j_Zh$. The structural maps glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] because $h$ is over $A^\prime$. Flatness of $Y^\prime$ follows from [def-weil-flat-morphism]: at each point its local structural map is that of one of the flat open pieces. After reduction to $A$, these pieces still form an open cover by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] (inverse images of a covering family cover). The maps $a:L_A\to Y_U$ and $e:Z_A\to Y_V$ agree on the overlap because $e_Wh_A=a_W$. They glue to $\alpha:Y^\prime_A\to Y$. Conversely the maps $j_{L,A}a^{-1}$ on $Y_U$ and $j_{Z,A}e^{-1}$ on $Y_V$ agree: $h_Aa_W^{-1}=e_W^{-1}$. They glue to an inverse. The composites are identities on the open covers, hence identities by uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The same uniqueness verifies that the maps are over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0DYZ, lemma-glueing, construction of the quasi-inverse; Schemes Tags 01JB and 01JC; explicit verification of the reduction marking

proof.text: Identify the special fibre of $Y^\prime$ with $X$ by $\iota\alpha_k$. The open $j_Z(Z)$ then has label $V$, since $\alpha j_{Z,A}=e$. Nilpotent reduction is a homeomorphism as in step 1, so this uniquely specifies the open $Y^\prime_V$: it equals $j_Z(Z)$. Define $\gamma:Y^\prime_V\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ by inverting this open-copy isomorphism. Restricting $\alpha j_{Z,A}=e$ gives $e\gamma_A=\alpha|_{Y_V}$. If $U$ is empty, the result is $Z$; if $V$ or $W$ is empty, the same gluing uses the unique empty overlap. No connectedness or dimension bound was used.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, second assertion: the prescribed-lift compatibility
